title: Initial-region physical scaffold
scope: Qualitative physical geography, hydrology, geomorphic sequence, coastal character, climate regime, and winter/summer pattern of Project Hearthway's initial region; usable within shared-setting ecology, location, culture, material exchange, and story development.
claims: Wet rocky uplands lie broadly west and northwest of a sheltered central lake basin; beyond an eastern or southeastern outlet gap, downstream lower marsh country leads toward a broken drowned coast.
The basin lake is freshwater and through-flowing: multiple rivers and streams feed it, and an outlet river drains it toward the sea.
The outlet leaves the basin through a narrow, naturally defensible gap.
The landscape preserves successive geomorphic phases: an ancient river basin was later reshaped by glaciation.
Ancient inundation formed the drowned coast; its broad regional outline is now stable, while storms can alter local channels and bars or remove small landforms.
Drowned valleys, tidal marshes, peat islands, sandbars, wooded islands, and narrow sea passages occur within the coastal mosaic.
The immediate region has a transitional maritime-continental climate.
Western windward terrain supports a major alien temperate-rainforest biome, while scattered damp refugia also occur within the basin.
Upland snow accumulates reliably and feeds a strong spring melt, while basin snow comes most years but can thaw and return several times within a winter.
Sheltered lake bays, wetlands, and slow river reaches freeze regularly; continuous surface ice across the lake's deeper central waters occurs only in unusually severe winters.
Sudden thaws can produce flooding, moving ice, and dangerous river crossings.
Summers are normally mild to warm, with long daylight and regular rain; occasional hotter dry spells can last several weeks, while severe drought remains uncommon.
The western rainforest and damp ravines usually remain moist during those dry spells, while basin open ground, habitat edges, and peaty margins can become dry enough to support surface fire.
boundaries: Britain, Doggerland, and Scandinavia are author-facing inspiration only and establish no Earth location, chronology, culture, species, language, or hidden connection.
Temperate rainforest describes climate-supported vegetation structure; its alien species, ancestry, anatomy, extent, productivity, in-world name, and human use remain undefined.

Within this record, defensible describes terrain potential only. WLD-LOCATION-001 later establishes a bounded initial ridge-spur settlement working landscape and combined spring-well-cistern water system; exact wall form, ownership, road dimensions, and hydrogeology remain outside this record.

Exact map scale, place names, distances, travel times, elevations, slopes, contours, river courses, lake form, quantitative outlet profile, gap dimensions, and coast shape remain undefined. WLD-GEOGRAPHY-002 later establishes only the outlet's qualitative mixed-reach feature sequence.
Exact geological dates, rock types, glacial sequence, soil map, mineral resources, inundation cause, former shorelines, and cultural consequences remain undefined.

Exact lake depth, volume, mixing, chemistry, water-level cycle, freeze duration, inflow count and discharge, outlet capacity, head of tide, freshwater tidal influence, salt-front position, and storm-surge reach remain undefined; the lake remains freshwater.
The lower basin floor remains distinct from downstream lower marsh and coastal country; this record does not move the existing crown corridor through the outlet gap or to the coast.
Continuous central-lake freezing means surface ice rather than a frozen water column.
Exact temperatures, rainfall, snowfall, prevailing winds, storm frequency, drought, fire, seasonal calendar, and day length remain undefined beyond the qualitative pattern in the claims.

WLD-ECOLOGY-006 later establishes broad qualitative lake productivity and two seasonal sea-lake migrant relationships, while WLD-ECOLOGY-010 later selects one organism-side outlet-passage choreography for the family-care migrant. WLD-GEOGRAPHY-002 later establishes a narrow bedrock throat and a downstream mixed reach containing irregular boulder steps, side shelves, and holding pockets. That qualitative sequence is only a candidate physical basis for passage attempts: exact feature dimensions and continuity, hydraulics, seasonal water states, salinity transition, route capacity, organism compatibility, passability, and passage success remain undefined; exact habitat distribution, quantitative productivity, species ranges, other transit modes, population scale and timing, other migrations, trade, imports, settlements beyond WLD-LOCATION-001's bounded initial-settlement landscape, cultures, histories, current events, and character knowledge also remain undefined.
This record establishes no magical climate cause, ecological reset, ambient spawning, ancient-doorway effect, or offworld connection.
story_implications: The protagonist's initial region can present a coherent gradient from wet rocky uplands through a sheltered lake basin to marshy lowlands and a broken drowned coast.
Snowmelt, variable ice, local flooding, storms, and occasional dry spells can support grounded seasonal pressures when later story records select exact events.
The outlet gap is a potential chokepoint, but any fortification, crossing, controller, route, toll, settlement, or conflict requires a separate accepted claim.
Later migrations, travel, imports, and tales can use this physical scaffold but must still establish exact routes, logistics, locality, evidence, and character knowledge.
The complete scaffold is author-side causal truth; characters know only the places, patterns, records, reports, and observations available to them.
system_implications: The selected landforms, hydrology, climate, coast, freeze-thaw cycle, flooding, and fire opportunity are ordinary world-level inputs under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D, not a System change.
No Mana weather engine, magical climate control, ambient spawning, ecological reset, inexhaustible resource, automatic recovery, or offworld mechanism is established.
research_questions: What exact dimensions, spacing, continuity, seasonal inundation, hydraulics, route capacity, and downstream salinity transition turn WLD-GEOGRAPHY-002's mixed outlet sequence into a viable or non-viable test of the WLD-ECOLOGY-010 passage requirement?
What rock, sediment, and glacial history produce the selected terrain, and what soil patterns result, without importing Earth chronology?
What quantitative seasonal water and energy balance supports the lake, snow, ice, floods, rainforest moisture, dry spells, and uncommon severe drought?
Which alien producer, decomposer, consumer, and habitat-forming families occupy each part of the regional gradient?
How do later approved migrations and human routes use or avoid the uplands, lake, outlet gap, marsh country, and coast?
What does each culture and viewpoint character know about the region, its weather, its drowned coast, and its geological past?
sources: Author selections across the guided regional geography and climate design on 2026-08-14

author_approval.evidence: Across guided design questions on 2026-08-14, the Author selected a freshwater through-flow lake and seaward outlet, replied 'defensible gap', and replied 'yes' to the transitional climate, western rainforest distribution, layered river-glacial origin, broadly stable drowned coast, winter pattern, summer pattern, and west-to-east regional arrangement.
